answers.explanation: The elastic potential energy becomes the stone's kinetic energy: ½Fx = ½mv². Thus F = mv²/x = 0.5 × 40²/0.20 = 4.0 × 10³ N.
The vertical components of the two equal handle forces support the bag: 2T cos 60° = 162 N, so T = 162 N.
For sliding friction, it is independent of apparent contact area, depends on the nature of the surfaces, and is proportional to the normal reaction. I, II and IV are correct.
Fresh water is less dense than salt water, so the ship must displace a greater volume and sits lower; the volume above the water surface decreases.
Since T is proportional to √L, halving the period makes the new length one-quarter of the original. L − L/4 = 1.5 m, giving L = 2.0 m.
At a point in a stationary liquid, pressure is equal in all directions (Pascal's principle).
In uniform circular motion, no work is done by the centripetal force and the centripetal force is directed towards the centre. II and IV are correct.
Acceleration is dv/dt. For v = 10 + 2t², a = 4t; at t = 5 s, a = 20 m/s².
Power P = Fv. Halving both force and velocity reduces power to one-quarter.
Efficiency = MA/VR, so MA = 0.75 × 5 = 3.75. Effort = load/MA = 150/3.75 = 40 N.
Acceleration = (4 − 0)/8 = 0.5 m/s². T − mg = ma, so T = 10(10 + 0.5) = 105 N.
Resolving the boat's velocity relative to the water and the stream gives the boat speed as 0.75/sin 30° = 1.50 m/s.
Stable interference fringes require coherent sources of the same frequency (and hence the same wavelength). I, II and III is the intended combination.
For reflection in a plane mirror, deviation = 2i. Thus i = 120°/2 = 60°.
The wet- and dry-bulb differences fall from 8°C to 7°C to 4°C, indicating that relative humidity increases steadily.
Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a denser medium to a less dense medium and strikes the boundary above the critical angle.
The waves on the wire are reflected at the fixed end and superpose with the incoming waves to form stationary transverse waves.
For a sonometer wire, f is proportional to the square root of tension. Doubling tension gives a new frequency of √2 f₀.
Apparent depth = real depth/refractive index ≈ 6.0/1.33 = 4.5 m.
Heat gained by the calorimeter and water is (80 + 420) × 10 = 5000 J. Equating this to 0.5c × 75 gives c ≈ 133 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.
The diagram is the maximum-minimum thermometer arrangement: P and R contain mercury indices, while Q contains alcohol.
An airtight cover prevents air circulation through the neck, reducing heat loss by convection.
The wave speed is fλ = 550 × 0.01 = 5.5 m/s and k = 2π/λ = 200π rad/m. Thus y = 0.15 sin[200π(x − 5.5t)].
Water has maximum density at about 4°C; as it is heated from 0°C to 30°C, its density first rises and then falls.
The process in which pressure causes ice to melt beneath the wire and the water refreezes behind it is regelation.
A potentiometer can measure a small cell internal resistance accurately by comparing potential differences without drawing appreciable current.
The electron's kinetic energy is ½mv² = ½ × 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ × (4 × 10⁷)². Dividing by e gives a potential difference of about 4.55 × 10³ V.
In a rare-to-dense transition, blue light is deviated most and red least. The rays a, b and c are therefore blue, yellow and red.
The capacitors are in parallel, so each has 20 V across it. QP = 5 μF × 20 V = 100 μC and QQ = 10 μF × 20 V = 200 μC.
An astronomical telescope uses an objective lens of long focal length and an eyepiece of short focal length, matching 500 cm and 5 cm.
For an ion passing undeflected through crossed electric and magnetic fields, qE = qvB, so v = E/B.
The series current is 2/(3 + 2 + 1) = 1/3 A. The p.d. across 3 Ω is 1 V and across 2 Ω is 2/3 V.
Magnification v/u = 24. With image distance v = 72 m, the slide distance u = 72/24 = 3.0 m.
Six cells aid and two oppose, giving a net of (6 − 2) × 2.0 V = 8 V.
For an inductor, XL = 2πfL. With f = 50/π Hz and L = 2 H, XL = 200 Ω.
1/64 = (1/2)⁶, so 120 years represents six half-lives. The half-life is 120/6 = 20 years.
Beta particles are charged and are deflected by both electric and magnetic fields.
In a pure semiconductor, each excited electron leaves a hole; the number of conduction electrons equals the number of holes.
Cell efficiency = external resistance/(external resistance + internal resistance) = 3/(3 + 1) = 75%.
The maximum electron kinetic energy is 5 eV − 3 eV = 2 eV, so the stopping potential is 2.0 V.
By Faraday's law, induced e.m.f. = N(dΦ/dt) = 200 × 0.08 = 16 V.
For the emitted x-ray photon, eV = hf. Thus V = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 1.6 × 10¹⁶)/(1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹) ≈ 66.3 V.
A fuse must be connected in the live wire; in the diagram this is position P.
The generator current is I = P/V = 3000/1500 = 2 A. Cable power loss = I²R = 2² × 20 = 80 W.
The maximum magnetic force is F = BIL = 0.5 × 0.8 × 2 = 0.8 N.
